submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole is a positional readout: its pre-activation (w.ln_2(h)+b) is dominated by GPT-2's learned absolute position embedding, so the first token of any prompt is silent whatever it is (pre-activation about +0.15, strength 0.000) and, on ordinary running prose, the peak over a prompt grows with its length - about 0.03 at 30 tokens, 0.08 at 60, 0.14 at 90 and 0.16-0.17 (the gelu_new dip maximum) from roughly 120 tokens on - while shifting position_ids by -400 moves that whole ramp 400 tokens later. The weaker token/context residual of the same pre-activation decides the rest: it pushes down on ordinary words and up on non-word tokens (digits, operators, single letters, '####'), so code and symbol-dense text need far more tokens to reach the dip (a 300-token code block peaks at 0.09, a 650-token one at 0.17 near position 420), and short prose prompts sit at the activity line rather than under it (median peak about 0.04 over 8-30-token sentences against the 0.25x-scale line of 0.028), which is why the 128-token scan's examples are weak scattered peaks on assorted common words (' remember', ' the', ' to', ' capital', ' often', ' while') with no coherent lexical class - that residual does not track token frequency, surprisal, next-token entropy, bigram probability or embedding norm.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
By the middle of the nineteenth century, the mapping of ocean depths had become one of the most ambitious projects in the physical sciences. Earlier charts had been compiled from the reports of sailors who lowered weighted lines over the side of a ship and counted the fathoms as the rope ran out. Those soundings were accurate in shallow water and almost useless in the open sea, where currents dragged the line sideways and the weight sometimes failed to reach the bottom at all. Naval officers learned to distrust their own numbers, and many of the figures printed on early charts were little better than guesses dressed up in careful handwriting.

The turning point came with the introduction of steam-powered vessels and the systematic survey cruises sponsored by navies and telegraph companies. A survey ship of the 1870s carried hundreds of miles of hemp rope, dozens of glass tubes for sampling sediment, and a crew trained to take readings in almost any weather. Each sounding required the ship to stop, hold position against wind and swell, and let the line descend for several minutes. Some stations took an hour to complete. The officers who kept the logs recorded not only depth but temperature, the colour and texture of the mud brought up on the sounding lead, and any fragments of shell or coral tangled in the tallow.

The results were surprising. The sea floor was not a smooth basin sloping gently away from the continents, as most naturalists had assumed. It was a landscape with ridges, plateaus, and trenches, and the sediments recovered from it contained the remains of organisms that no one had ever seen alive. Debate followed about how such creatures could survive in total darkness under enormous pressure. Some argued that the deep ocean was a frozen void in which nothing could live; others pointed to the living animals brought up in the dredges and insisted that the abyss supported a fauna of its own. The argument was settled only gradually, as more samples accumulated and the anatomical work caught up with the collecting.

What the surveyors could not have known was how much their slow, improvised measurements would matter a century later. The contours they sketched by hand became the first rough outline of plate tectonics, and the sediment cores they saved are still studied by researchers interested in ancient climates. A chart compiled by a tired officer at the end of a long watch has sometimes turned out to be the only surviving record of a coastline that has since changed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A passage of over 512 tokens with the content deep inside, testing the long-context claim that the ramp holds and the peak sits at the gelu_new dip maximum of about 0.16-0.17 rather than decaying.
